lessons.title: Managing resources across the farm
lessons.html:
Taking a management role

In this workplace module you manage resources for a section of the farm, or the whole farm on a small operation, under a mentor or farm manager. Unlike earlier modules, you are now expected to plan, allocate and control resources, and to report on performance, not only to carry out checks.

Areas of responsibility

  • Water: plan use against supply and authorisation, monitor quality and discharge.
  • Stock: keep accurate numbers, biomass and densities; plan movements and harvests.
  • Feed and consumables: forecast needs, set reorder points, procure, store and control issues.
  • Equipment and infrastructure: maintain the asset register and maintenance schedule; plan replacements.
  • People: rosters, task allocation, training and safety.
  • Budget: track spending against the budget for your area.

A monthly management cycle

  1. Plan: confirm the production plan for the month and the resources it needs.
  2. Allocate: assign staff, equipment and inputs to units and tasks.
  3. Monitor: use daily and weekly records to track usage and performance.
  4. Control: correct deviations quickly, such as reducing feed when appetite falls or fixing leaks.
  5. Report: summarise results, variances and actions for the manager.
  6. Improve: propose and trial changes based on what the figures show.

Decisions under pressure

Real farms face constraints: a drought lowers dam levels, feed prices rise, a key staff member resigns, load shedding increases. Document each constraint, the options you considered, the decision taken with the manager's approval, and the result. This shows the judgement assessors look for at this level.

Compliance

Ensure your area complies with the farm's water use authorisation, OHS Act 85 of 1993 safety requirements, labour conditions, and any permits for the species farmed. Raise compliance gaps with the manager in writing.

lessons.title: Reporting performance and showing competence
lessons.html:
A monthly resource report

Prepare a concise report each month. Managers need facts, comparisons and recommendations, not long narratives.

SectionContent
ProductionBiomass, growth, survival, harvests vs plan
FeedTonnes used, FCR, stock on hand, cost per kg produced
Water and energyUse per kg produced, quality issues, outages
EquipmentBreakdowns, downtime, repairs, items for replacement
PeopleAttendance, overtime, training, incidents
BudgetActual vs budget, main variances and reasons
ActionsProblems, decisions taken, recommendations

Analysing variances

For each significant difference from plan, explain the cause and the response. For example: 'Feed cost 12% over budget because grower feed price increased and FCR rose in Pond 3 after a low-oxygen event. Aeration schedule revised and Pond 3 ration reduced.' Figures in examples are illustrative.

Making recommendations

Support recommendations with simple cost-benefit figures: cost, expected saving or extra income, payback period, risks. Examples include replacing an old pump, adding a feed store, investing in a generator, or changing a fingerling supplier.

Leading the team

Resource management depends on people following procedures. Brief the team on the plan, explain why targets matter, give feedback on records and recognise good work. Correct unsafe practices immediately.

Portfolio of evidence

  • Monthly plans and resource reports you prepared.
  • Calculations: reorder points, feed forecasts, KPIs, payback.
  • Records of decisions under constraint and their outcomes.
  • Mentor or manager testimony on your performance.
  • Evidence of improvements you initiated.

All evidence must be your own, current and sufficient to show consistent management over time.

Key points

  • Plan, allocate, monitor, control, report and improve every month.
  • Report facts and variances with clear causes and actions.
  • Support recommendations with cost-benefit figures.
  • Document decisions made under constraints.
  • Keep your area compliant and raise gaps in writing.
